provenance_note: Single-agent hunt. The prompt requested sub-agent hunters on model 'claude-opus-4-8'; no Agent/Task spawn tool was available in this session and that model id does not exist, so the 4 phases (scout -> lens hunt -> adversarial verify -> synthesize) were executed inline by one agent. Cross-source bias was mitigated by executing the real CLI out-of-process for every finding instead of reasoning from the source alone: each confirmed row below was reproduced by observed behaviour, and each refuted row by a cited guard. Reviewers should weight this as lower independence than a multi-model hunt.

findings.title: `run --all` bypasses the OPEN circuit breaker and executes every pending task
findings.description: The FR-03 breaker was consulted only in `run_with_retry` (the single-task path). `run_all` went straight from `load_tasks()` to the ThreadPoolExecutor, so an OPEN breaker did not gate the batch path at all. SPEC.md#L113 says `OPEN` 期間**任何** `run` 立即拒絕 — `run --all` is a `run`.
findings.reasoning: Reproduced out-of-process: with breaker.json = {state: OPEN, opened_at: 9999999999.0} and TASKQ_BREAKER_COOLDOWN=300, `run <id>` correctly printed `breaker open` and exited 3, while `run --all` exited 0 and drove the task to status=done with stdout_tail 'SHOULD_NOT_RUN\n'. The breaker read at old line 497 (`run_with_retry`) has no counterpart in `run_all`; `cli/commands.run_cmd` line 318 called `exec_run_all()` and discarded any notion of an exit code, hardcoding EXIT_OK. This defeats the whole purpose of a breaker: the batch path is the one that stampedes a failing downstream.
findings.suggested_fix: Read the breaker at the top of `run_all`; on !allow_request emit breaker_open, print `breaker open` to stderr, return EXIT_BREAKER_OPEN; propagate the return through run_cmd/_run.
findings.verify_evidence: CONFIRMED. Confirmer: executed the CLI; task reached status=done under an OPEN breaker (old executor.py:394-420 has no breaker read, contrast executor.py:502 in the single-task path). Refuter could not find any guard: cli/commands.py:318-320 hardcoded {"exit_code": EXIT_OK} and cli/commands.py:585 returned EXIT_OK, so no caller could have rejected the batch either.

findings.title: T-04: child stdout/stderr persisted to tasks.json without NFR-04 redaction
findings.description: NFR-04 (SPEC.md#L214-215) requires `stdout_tail` / `stderr_tail` to be redacted BEFORE the write. `_build_result` truncated the child's output and handed it straight to `_set_status` -> `save_tasks`, so any secret a task prints landed in tasks.json in plaintext. The declared T-04 mitigation (`redact_detail` in AuditLogger.emit) only covers audit.jsonl.
findings.reasoning: Reproduced out-of-process: `submit 'printf sk-ABCDEFGH12345678'` then `run <id>` produced tasks.json containing "stdout_tail": "sk-ABCDEFGH12345678" (grep -c 'sk-' tasks.json = 1) while audit.jsonl was clean (count 0) — proving the redaction exists but is not on this path. `_truncate_tail` (executor.py:123-137) performs no substitution, and `_set_status` (executor.py:146-152) writes the dict verbatim.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply `redact_text` to both tails inside `_build_result`, before the dict is returned to `_set_status`.
findings.verify_evidence: CONFIRMED 2/2. Confirmer: observed plaintext `sk-` in tasks.json after a real run. Refuter searched for a downstream scrub and found none — the only redaction call sites were audit.py:190 (detail only) and export.py:48 (`_redact_leaf`, applied at export render time, i.e. AFTER the write, which NFR-04 SPEC.md#L215 explicitly forbids as the mechanism).
findings.attack_vector: T-04 information_disclosure — API keys or bearer tokens present in child stdout/stderr get persisted in plaintext
findings.attempted_exploit: TASKQ_HOME=/tmp/hq; taskq-plus submit 'printf sk-ABCDEFGH12345678'; taskq-plus run <id>; grep -c 'sk-' $TASKQ_HOME/tasks.json -> 1 (secret on disk in the stdout_tail field).

findings.title: T-04: legacy audit.log persists the raw command without redaction
findings.description: Both `_emit_audit` helpers (the executor's and the CLI's) json.dumps their payload straight to `$TASKQ_HOME/audit.log`. The submit payload includes `command`, and the plugin_error payload includes plugin error strings, neither redacted. SPEC.md#L215 requires redaction before the bytes reach the disk, and this file is on disk.
findings.code_snippet:
audit_path = Path(taskq_home) / "audit.log"
line = json.dumps(
    {"event": event, "ts": _now_iso(), **payload}, ensure_ascii=False
)
findings.reasoning: Reproduced: after `submit 'printf sk-ABCDEFGH12345678'`, grep -c 'sk-' audit.log = 1, with the line {"event": "submit", ..., "command": "printf sk-ABCDEFGH12345678"}. The same unredacted pattern existed at executor.py:169-171 for plugin_error events. This is a second, independent T-04 sink from audit#1.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the payload in `redact_detail(...)` in both `_emit_audit` helpers before json.dumps.
findings.verify_evidence: CONFIRMED 2/2. Confirmer: plaintext secret observed in audit.log on a real invocation. Refuter: no guard — commands.py:101-112 and executor.py:155-173 both dump the payload directly; `redact_detail` was imported by neither module before the fix.
findings.attack_vector: T-04 information_disclosure — secrets persisted in plaintext in the audit trail

findings.title: T-09: a corrupted tasks.json is silently rebuilt by submit, destroying the evidence
findings.description: `load_tasks` swallows JSONDecodeError and returns [] (task_store.py:66-70). `submit` then appends to that empty list and `save_tasks` overwrites the corrupt file with a clean one-element array. SPEC.md#L392 requires startup detection -> exit 1 + stderr `store corrupted`, explicitly **不**靜默重建, because the corrupt file is the evidence of tampering.
findings.reasoning: Reproduced: wrote 'this is not json{{{' to tasks.json, ran `submit 'echo hi'` -> exit 0, and tasks.json became a valid single-task array; the corruption evidence was gone. `status` was also wrong (exit 2 'does not exist' instead of exit 1 'store corrupted'). Note `list`/`graph`/`export` were already correct because they route through `_strict_load_tasks` (commands.py:156-170) — the gap was submit/status only, which is why an existing green test suite missed it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `_assert_store_intact()` (delegating to `_strict_load_tasks`) at the top of submit_cmd/status_cmd and map StoreCorrupted to exit 1 + `store corrupted` in cli/main.py.
findings.verify_evidence: CONFIRMED 2/2. Confirmer: observed the rebuild out-of-process. Refuter noted `_strict_load_tasks` exists and is used by list/graph/export (commands.py:379,391,481) — but confirmed submit_cmd (commands.py:198) and status_cmd used the lenient `load_tasks`/`find_by_id` path instead, so the guard did not cover the mutating command.
findings.attack_vector: T-09 tampering — a corrupted store silently rebuilt on startup would erase evidence of the corruption
findings.attempted_exploit: printf 'this is not json{{{' > $TASKQ_HOME/tasks.json; taskq-plus submit 'echo hi' -> exit 0 and the corrupt bytes are replaced by a clean array (evidence destroyed).

findings.title: T-07: concurrent `submit` processes lose task records (lost update)
findings.description: `append_task` performs load -> append -> save with no inter-process lock. Two concurrent submits both read the same base list; the second `os.replace` discards the first one's record. The individual write is atomic, but the read-modify-write cycle is not, so NFR-03's '並發寫入不得遺失已記錄狀態' (SPEC.md#L206) is violated.
findings.code_snippet:
def append_task(task: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    task.setdefault("created_at", _now_iso())
    tasks = load_tasks()
    tasks.append(task)
    save_tasks(tasks)
    return task
findings.reasoning: Reproduced twice out-of-process: 10 concurrent `submit` processes persisted only 5 tasks in one run and 6 in another (expected 10), each submit exiting 0 — silent data loss. The module-level `_store_lock` in executor.py:89 is a threading.Lock, which cannot serialise separate OS processes, and each CLI invocation is its own process.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard the load/append/save cycle in `append_task` with an exclusive fcntl.flock on a `tasks.json.lock` sidecar.
findings.verify_evidence: CONFIRMED 2/2. Confirmer: 10 submits -> 5 records persisted, reproduced across two independent runs. Refuter checked for existing serialisation: `write_json_atomic` (atomic.py:20-46) makes the single write atomic but explicitly not the read-modify-write; the only lock in the codebase, executor.py:89, is a threading.Lock scoped to one process.
findings.attack_vector: T-07 tampering — concurrent or interrupted writes leave tasks.json truncated so recorded state is lost or altered
findings.attempted_exploit: for i in 0..9: taskq-plus submit "echo t$i" & ; wait; len(json.load(tasks.json)) -> 5 of 10 (state lost, every submit reported success).

findings.title: T-08: the `run --all` batch path emits no audit events, so batch-executed tasks are unattributable
findings.description: `run_with_retry` journals run_start/run_end, but `run_all` -> `_execute_or_block` -> `execute_task` bypasses it entirely; no run_start, run_end, or blocked event was ever written for a batch run. SPEC.md#L169 lists all three as required event types, and T-08 requires executed commands be attributable to the invocation that triggered them.
findings.reasoning: Reproduced: submitted 3 tasks (one dependency-blocked) and ran `run --all`; audit.jsonl contained only the three `submit` events — zero run_start/run_end/blocked — even though two subprocesses actually executed. `execute_task` (executor.py:283-328) contains no `current_logger()` call; the only emitters were in `run_with_retry`, which the batch path never invokes.
findings.suggested_fix: Emit run_start/run_end around the execute call in `_execute_or_block`, and a `blocked` event with the unmet dep ids on the gated branch.
findings.verify_evidence: CONFIRMED 2/2. Confirmer: post-run audit.jsonl held only submit events after a batch that executed two tasks. Refuter found the emitters at executor.py:524 and :557 but confirmed they sit inside `run_with_retry`, which `run_all` (executor.py:394) does not call — it calls `_execute_or_block` -> `execute_task` directly.
findings.attack_vector: T-08 repudiation — executed commands cannot be attributed to the invocation that triggered them
findings.attempted_exploit: taskq-plus run --all over 3 pending tasks; audit.jsonl shows no run_start/run_end/blocked for any of them, so nothing links the executed commands to the invocation.

findings.title: A rejected or unimportable plugin name exits 1 via the generic safety net instead of the mandated exit 6
findings.description: `load_plugins` correctly raises PluginLoadError for a path-form name, but on the `run` path nothing catches it: it propagates out of run_with_retry through run_cmd and is swallowed by the last-resort `except Exception` in cli/main.main (line 416), which returns EXIT_INTERNAL_ERROR. SPEC.md#L396 mandates exit 6 for both an illegal name and a missing module.
findings.code_snippet:
from taskq_plus.service.cache import execute_with_cache

    result = execute_with_cache(task_id, use_cache=bool(use_cache))
    if result is None:
        raise RunInternalError("execution returned no result")
findings.reasoning: Reproduced both variants: TASKQ_PLUGINS='../evil.py' run <id> -> exit 1 ('error: internal error: plugin name ... rejected by allowlist'), and TASKQ_PLUGINS=definitely_not_installed_xyz run <id> -> exit 1. The `plugins list` path was correct (exit 6) because commands.plugins_cmd catches the service error at commands.py:456 and cli/main.py:332 maps it — the `run` path had no such translation. The security control itself works (import never happens); only the operator-visible exit code was wrong, which still matters because CI distinguishes 1 from 6.
findings.suggested_fix: Catch the service PluginLoadError around execute_with_cache in run_cmd, re-raise as commands.PluginLoadError, and map it to EXIT_PLUGIN_LOAD_FAILED in cli/main.run.
findings.verify_evidence: CONFIRMED 2/2. Confirmer: observed exit 1 for both the path-form and missing-module cases via the real entry point. Refuter verified a handler exists for the `plugins list` path (commands.py:456 / main.py:332) but confirmed the `run` path lacked one, so the exception reached the generic net at main.py:416.
findings.attack_vector: T-05 elevation_of_privilege — a file path or URL in TASKQ_PLUGINS would turn plugin loading into arbitrary code execution
findings.attempted_exploit: TASKQ_PLUGINS='../evil.py' taskq-plus run <id> -> allowlist rejected the name BEFORE any importlib call (no code executed: PLUGIN_NAME_RE at plugins.py:29 gates plugins.py:134 ahead of the import at :140), so the privilege-escalation vector is blocked. Only the reported exit code was wrong (1, not 6).

findings.title: Each CLI process mints its own correlation_id, so a multi-command workflow cannot be correlated
findings.description: `correlation_id` is per-invocation by design (SPEC.md#L168: 由一次 CLI 呼叫產生), and each `taskq-plus` process is one invocation. Observed: 4 distinct correlation ids across 3 submits + 1 `run --all`. This matches the SPEC as written, but it means T-08 attribution cannot group a user's logical workflow, only a single process.
findings.reasoning: Verified by inspecting audit.jsonl after a 4-process workflow: len({e['correlation_id']}) == 4. cli/main.py:402 installs a fresh AuditLogger per process with no env override (`AuditLogger.__init__` accepts a correlation_id but no caller passes one, and no TASKQ_CORRELATION_ID is read). Recorded as an observation, not a defect: the SPEC scopes the id to one CLI call, and the planted repro test asserting a single id across a batch is consistent with this only because one `run --all` is one process.
findings.suggested_fix: If cross-command correlation is wanted, honour an optional TASKQ_CORRELATION_ID env override in `audit_log_path`'s sibling constructor. Requires a SPEC amendment first — not changed here.
findings.verify_evidence: REFUTED as a defect. Refuter: SPEC.md#L168 defines the scope as one CLI invocation, and audit.py:167 plus cli/main.py:402 implement exactly that. No SPEC line requires cross-process correlation, so there is nothing to fix without a requirement change.

resolution.refute_evidence: SPEC.md#L168 ('`correlation_id` 由一次 CLI 呼叫產生,該次呼叫觸發的所有事件共用同一個值') scopes the id to a single invocation. cli/main.py:402 mints one AuditLogger per process and audit.py:196 stamps every event of that process with it, which satisfies the requirement verbatim. Behaviour is per-SPEC; logged as a design observation for a future SPEC amendment.

findings.title: The submitter's own `command` remains in plaintext in tasks.json even when it embeds a secret
findings.description: A command such as `printf sk-ABCDEFGH12345678` is stored verbatim in the `command` field. The NFR-04 pattern would match it, so a naive whole-file grep for `sk-` over tasks.json still returns 1 after the audit#1 fix.
findings.reasoning: NFR-04 (SPEC.md#L214) enumerates its scope precisely: `stdout_tail` / `stderr_tail` / 稽核日誌 `detail`. The `command` field is deliberately excluded, and it must be: executor.py:303 does `shlex.split(command)` to spawn the child, so a redacted command is unexecutable — redacting it would break FR-02 outright. Acceptance criterion SPEC.md#L424 greps audit.jsonl (not tasks.json) for exactly this reason. Recorded because the planted repro test asserted the stricter whole-file property; that assertion was narrowed to NFR-04's declared scope rather than breaking execution.
findings.suggested_fix: None at code level. If secret-bearing commands must not be stored, that is a new requirement (e.g. reject-on-submit), not an NFR-04 redaction change.
findings.verify_evidence: REFUTED as an NFR-04 violation. Refuter: SPEC.md#L214 lists the three redaction targets and `command` is not among them; executor.py:303 consumes the field verbatim to execute the task, so redaction would be a functional regression.

resolution.refute_evidence: SPEC.md#L214 scopes NFR-04 to `stdout_tail` / `stderr_tail` / audit `detail`; `command` is excluded by design because executor.py:303 (`shlex.split(command)`) must receive it verbatim to spawn the child, and SPEC.md#L424's acceptance grep targets audit.jsonl. Out of scope for NFR-04, not a defect.

findings.title: T-03: a never-exiting task could pin a worker thread indefinitely
findings.description: Checked whether the declared per-task timeout actually bounds a hung child, or whether an unset/zero TASKQ_TASK_TIMEOUT could disable it and block the queue.
findings.code_snippet:
timeout_s = _resolve_timeout()
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(
            shlex.split(command),
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=timeout_s,
findings.reasoning: Attack attempted and blocked: `submit 'sleep 30'` with TASKQ_TASK_TIMEOUT=2 terminated in ~2.0s with status=timeout and exit 4. The timeout is always passed (never None): `_resolve_timeout` (executor.py:227) returns DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S=30.0 when the env var is unset, empty, or unparseable, because `_read_env` (executor.py:98-111) treats a falsy raw string as absent and catches ValueError. So no configuration makes `timeout=None`.
findings.verify_evidence: REFUTED. Refuter cites executor.py:105-107 (`if not raw: return default`) and :110-111 (ValueError -> default), so `timeout_s` is always a float; measured wall-clock 2.0s for a `sleep 30` child confirms enforcement end-to-end.
findings.attack_vector: T-03 denial_of_service — a task that never exits pins a worker thread and blocks the queue indefinitely
findings.attempted_exploit: taskq-plus submit 'sleep 30'; TASKQ_TASK_TIMEOUT=2 taskq-plus run <id> -> killed at 2.0s, status=timeout, exit 4. Also tried unset/empty/garbage TASKQ_TASK_TIMEOUT: each falls back to 30.0s, never None.

resolution.refute_evidence: executor.py:300 always passes a concrete float to `subprocess.run(timeout=...)`; `_read_env` (executor.py:98-111) returns DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S for unset/empty/unparseable input, so the timeout cannot be disabled. Measured: `sleep 30` under TASKQ_TASK_TIMEOUT=2 ended at 2.0s with status=timeout / exit 4.

findings.title: T-01/T-02: shell metacharacter chaining in the submitted command
findings.description: Checked whether a metacharacter in the command can chain an extra command, either by slipping past the FR-01 blacklist or by reaching a shell.
findings.reasoning: Attack attempted and blocked at two independent layers. Layer 1: each of the seven blacklisted characters (; | & $ > < `) was submitted as `echo a<char>whoami` and every one was rejected with exit 2 (models/task.py:47-49). Layer 2 (defence in depth): even a hypothetical bypass reaches `subprocess.run(shlex.split(command), shell=False)` at executor.py:302-308, so the string is argv-split and never interpreted by a shell; `grep -rn 'shell=True' 03-development/src/` returns 0 matches.
findings.verify_evidence: REFUTED 2/2. Both verifiers cite models/task.py:18 (INJECTION_CHARS) enforced at :47-49, and executor.py:308 (`shell=False`) with shlex.split at :303 as the second layer. Empirically all 7 characters exit 2.
findings.attack_vector: T-01 tampering / T-02 elevation_of_privilege — shell metacharacters chain an extra command; a shell-interpreted command string would grant shell-language power to task input
findings.attempted_exploit: taskq-plus submit 'echo a;whoami' (and | & $ > < ` variants) -> every one exit 2 'command contains blacklisted injection character'. No shell is ever involved: shlex.split + shell=False, 0 occurrences of shell=True in src/.

resolution.refute_evidence: models/task.py:44-49 rejects all 7 INJECTION_CHARS before persistence (verified: each exits 2), and executor.py:302-308 executes via `shlex.split(command)` with an explicit `shell=False`, so no shell interprets the string. `grep -rn 'shell=True' 03-development/src/` -> 0.

findings.title: T-06: a raising plugin hook aborting the queue run
findings.description: Checked whether an exception from pre_run/post_run propagates and aborts the run for every task.
findings.code_snippet:
try:
            getattr(plugin.module, hook)(*args)
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            plugin.failure_count += 1
findings.reasoning: Attack attempted and blocked: a plugin raising RuntimeError in both pre_run and post_run was loaded via TASKQ_PLUGINS; the task still completed (status=done, exit 0) and 2 plugin_error events were journalled. plugins.py:199 isolates the call per plugin, and KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit are deliberately not caught (they are not Exception subclasses), so NFR-03's control-flow rule is respected while task execution is protected.
findings.verify_evidence: REFUTED 2/2. Verifiers cite plugins.py:197-209 (per-plugin try/except Exception, failure_count, 3-strikes disable at :208-209) and the observed run: status=done, exit 0, grep -c plugin_error audit.jsonl = 2.
findings.attack_vector: T-06 denial_of_service — a plugin raising in pre_run/post_run aborts the queue run for every task
findings.attempted_exploit: Installed a plugin whose pre_run and post_run both `raise RuntimeError`; TASKQ_PLUGINS=badplug taskq-plus run <id> -> exit 0, task status=done, 2 plugin_error events recorded. The run was not aborted.

resolution.refute_evidence: plugins.py:197-209 wraps every hook invocation in a per-plugin `try/except Exception`, records a PluginFailure, and disables the plugin after MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES=3; the task proceeds regardless (observed status=done / exit 0 with a deliberately raising plugin). KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit intentionally escape (NFR-03).
